title: Storage classes: standard, infrequent access, Glacier and Deep Archive

videos.script: Lesson 1 put Quitanda's files in a bucket and never asked what kind of shelf they sat on. {{shelf}} Every object in S3 has a storage class. Standard is the default. Five others cost less to keep, and one moves your files between tiers by itself. {{classes}} The catch is the door. The cheaper the shelf, the more it costs to take something back off it, or the longer you wait for it. {{door}} In this lesson you write one file into four classes and try to read each one back. Two of them refuse. {{refuse}} You restore an archived file, and watch moto finish in a second what takes S3 up to two days. {{restore}} Then a short program prices a terabyte for a year in each class, and what reading it back once would cost. {{year}} By the end you can look at a set of files, ask how often they are read and how soon they are needed, and name their class. {{end}}
